short: Carbon distribution in multi-phase gamma-TiAl based alloys a
title: Carbon distribution in multi-phase gamma-TiAl based alloys and its influence on mechanical properties and phase formation

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Where carbon sits among gamma, alpha2 and beta-o, and what that does, has not been measured. Resolving the carbon distribution phase by phase should explain both the hardness changes and the phase selection.
states.detail: Absorbed: n2 (HYP/gap), n3 (HYP/hypothesis), n4 (DES/base_system), n5 (DES/modification), n6 (DES/method), n7 (DES/variable_sweep), n8 (PRC/forming), n9 (PRC/treatment)

states.title: Structure state
states.head: TNM is predominantly globular; TNM0.75C carries coarse lamellar colonies alongside globular grains. Carbon cuts the beta-o fraction from 19% to 2% and raises alpha2 from 11% to 37%.
states.detail: Absorbed: n10 (STR/microstructure/shape), n11 (STR/phase/fraction), n12 (STR/chemistry/composition), n13 (STR/interface), n14 (STR/phase/identity). Premises: Orientation relationship <111>beta-o {110}beta-o parallel to [0001]omega-o {11-20}omega-o

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: Interstitial carbon in gamma and alpha2 strains the lattice and impedes dislocation glide, hardening both phases. Carbon raises gamma hardness from 7.5 to 8.5 GPa and alpha2 hardness from 8.7 to 9.9 GPa.
states.detail: Absorbed: n15 (MEC/pathway), n16 (PRP/value), n17 (PRP/value), n18 (MEC/identification), n19 (MEC/pathway). Premises: Solid-solution hardening scales as the square root of the solute concentration

states.title: Performance state
states.head: Carbon-bearing TNM has higher strength and creep resistance at service temperature

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: Where the carbon goes sets both the hardening of gamma and alpha2 and the suppression of omega-o in beta-o

nodes.title: SEM:BSE, F1
nodes.head: BSE: TNM is globular with a bright beta-o network along most boundaries; TNM0.75C mixes coarse lamellar colonies with globular grains and shows only isolated bright specks
nodes.solves: TNM is predominantly globular; TNM0.75C carries coarse lamellar colonies alongside globular grains
nodes.note: both at a 30 um scale bar; in F1a the bright beta-o forms an interconnected network between the arrowed gamma and alpha2 grains, in F1b it survives only as a few isolated white specks. That near-disappearance is the clearest difference in the pair. Roughly half of the F1b field is still globular, so the C-bearing alloy is not 'largely lamellar'.
nodes.necessity_reason: S1 keeps shown support from o2, o3, o6, o7 after removal.

nodes.title: TEM:brightfield, F4
nodes.head: TEM: the TNM beta-o grain is filled with fine speckled contrast while the TNM0.75C beta-o grain is featureless
nodes.solves: Fine omega-o precipitates fill the beta-o of TNM and are absent from the beta-o of TNM0.75C
nodes.note: scale bars 1 um (F4a) and 0.5 um (F4b), so the two views are at different magnifications; the speckle is at the limit of resolution at 1 um
nodes.necessity_reason: S1 keeps shown support from o1, o2, o3, o7 after removal.

nodes.title: APT, F2
nodes.head: APT tip: blue C atoms crowd the gamma volume and the isoconcentration surface, while the beta-o volume is nearly bare of them
nodes.solves: Carbon partitions strongly: about 1.2 at.% in alpha2, 0.3 at.% in gamma and almost none in beta-o
nodes.op: assess spatial distribution, replot derived series

nodes.title: MECH:nanoindentation, F3
nodes.head: Hardness histograms shift right with C: gamma from a sharp 7.4 GPa mode to a broad mode near 8.4, alpha2 from ~9.0 to ~9.9 GPa
nodes.solves: Carbon raises gamma hardness from 7.5 to 8.5 GPa and alpha2 hardness from 8.7 to 9.9 GPa
nodes.note: the distributions overlap heavily (TNM gamma spans 7.0-8.7 GPa, TNM0.75C gamma 7.3-9.6), and the frequency axes carry no counts, so this is a mean shift rather than a separation
nodes.detail: o4: Hardness histograms shift right with C: gamma from a sharp 7.4 GPa mode to a broad mode near 8.4, alpha2 from ~9.0 to ~9.9 GPa

nodes.head: The beta-o histogram moves the other way: mode ~10.0 GPa with a tail to 11.5 in TNM, mode ~8.9 GPa and narrow in TNM0.75C
nodes.solves: Carbon instead softens the beta-o phase, from about 10.0 to 8.9 GPa
nodes.note: F3c and F3f share the 8.0-12.0 GPa axis, so the shift is directly comparable; the TNM distribution is also much wider

nodes.title: APT, APT:proximity, F5
nodes.head: APT reconstruction: Mo-poor channels thread through a Mo-rich matrix, matching the omega-o plates seen by t-EBSD. Mo proximity histogram: ~0.4 at.% inside omega-o, a 4.7 at.% maximum about 3 nm into beta-o, settling near 3.0 at.%
nodes.solves: Shrinking the beta-o fraction concentrates Mo in it, and omega-o cannot nucleate because it must reject Mo into that matrix
nodes.op: assess spatial distribution, read characteristic point, replot derived series
nodes.note: isoconcentration surfaces are drawn at 1 at.% Mo in F5b; the channels are the omega-o, which the surfaces exclude values read off the F5c ordinate; the maximum is marked cmax, and the far-field beta-o level is well below it
